messages:
maya: heads-up — canary FP8/INT8 mix rollout shows perf regressions + structured-output breakage on the longctx eval suite. eval delta ~+2.9% (regression), hallucination rate up, and a few json fields are missing in outputs. attaching quick notes.

jordan: :eyes: do we have profiler traces & which kernels got selected? is this across dedicated and hosted canaries?

maya: hosted canary only. profiler snapshot (trimmed):
```
PROFILER SUMMARY
timestamp: 1748604300
avg_token_latency: baseline 24ms -> canary 34ms
p50_kernel_time: +41%
kernel_choice: fp8_fast_gemm chosen for layers 0-9
fallback_kernel: int8_precise for layers 10+
kv_cache_hits: 81/100 (baseline 94/100)
batch_shape: mixed seq lengths (8/64/1024)
```

liam: mixed seq lengths + batching heuristics = risk. selector probably picked fp8_fast_gemm because it was faster on short seq bins. but when long ctx steps hit, numerical behavior shifted. any per-layer quant stats?

maya: pasted per-layer quant stats (small):
```
LAYER 7: scale_mean 0.012 -> 0.009, clip_ratio 0.02 -> 0.14
LAYER 8: scale_mean 0.008 -> 0.007, zero_points stable
LAYER 12: quant_error_rms +0.6 -> +1.8
```

sophia: clip_ratio jumping to 0.14 on L7 is suspect — likely calibration mismatch when mixing fp8 kernel path with int8 neighbors. structured outputs (json keys) tended to break when L7 produced slightly different logits for separators.

andre: quick repro suggestion: (1) force kernel selector to prefer fp8_precise for canary; (2) run eval with batcher forced to uniform seq_len bins (avoid mixing short+long). can you try both?

maya: working on it. launching canary with KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fp8_precise and BATCH_BUCKETING=uniform_seq. will run longctx eval.

ci-bot: deploy triggered — canary update id: rwd-canary-2145, env[KERNEL_OVERRIDE]=fp8_precise, BATCH_BUCKETING=uniform_seq :rocket:

(20m later)

maya: results: with fp8_precise override + uniform batching -> eval delta drops to +0.2%, hallucinations back near baseline, json fields restored. token latency slightly higher (+6%) but within SLO.

jordan: ok that's a strong signal. summary: kernel selection heuristic preferred fp8_fast_gemm for mixed batches; that path has lower numeric stability on specific layers (L7) when sequence-length mixing occurs. compounded by kv-cache warming drop (hit rate down) which amplified drift.

liam: next steps: 1) add a safety guard in kernel selector to prefer the precise fp8 path when structured-output or json-mode flagged; 2) tune batcher to avoid mixing very short and very long sequences in same micro-batch; 3) add per-layer calibration sanity check (clip_ratio threshold) to block fast_gemm selection if exceeded; 4) add a short-term canary rollback plan.

sophia: i'll draft the selector patch and a unit test that simulates mixed seq histograms + calibration anomaly. want to make the safety guard opt-in for 1 week then default on.

andre: also add a telemetry alert: if kv_cache hit_rate drops >10% vs baseline after kernel switch, auto-fallback to previous kernel. That would catch this earlier.

maya: agreed. i'll create the rollout PR and link tests. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: note: canary metrics stored at http://internal.metrics/rwd/canary/2145

maya: filing follow-up task: ENG-RUNTIME-2312 "kernel-selector: add structured-output safety and clip-ratio guard". assigning to sophia + liam. closing triage for now.
